name: DropShield Origin Assertion
description: Language-neutral contract and deterministic test vectors for DropShield origin assertions. An origin assertion is a short-lived, HMAC-SHA256-signed proof issued internally by DropShield.Api after a protected commerce mutation has passed all upstream checks (rate limiting, admission, admission proof, action proof, replay, reservation, behavioural policy). It is forwarded to the protected commerce origin (for example, the Adobe Commerce connector) in a dedicated internal header and is never generated or accepted from a client.

wireFormat.payloadEncoding: UTF-8 JSON, camelCase field names, no property reordering required by verifiers (verifiers must re-derive the signature from the exact payload segment bytes, not from re-serialized JSON)
wireFormat.signature: HMAC-SHA256(key = shared origin assertion signing key, message = signingInput)

payloadFields.kid: string, key identifier for the active signing key
payloadFields.drop: string, protected drop/product identifier the assertion authorises
payloadFields.action: string, lowercase action name, e.g. "cart" or "checkout"
payloadFields.method: string, uppercase HTTP method of the protected request, e.g. "POST"
payloadFields.route: string, canonical protected route template, e.g. "POST /api/cart"
payloadFields.bodyHash: string, base64url(SHA-256(raw forwarded request body)); SHA-256 of an empty byte array when there is no body
payloadFields.jti: string, base64url-encoded random assertion identifier (not required to be validated for uniqueness by the origin; replay protection is enforced upstream by DropShield, not by the origin connector)
payloadFields.exp: integer, expiry unix timestamp; exp - iat must not exceed the configured assertion lifetime (seconds, single digits to low tens)

steps: Split on '.' into exactly 3 parts; reject otherwise.
Base64url-decode parts 1 and 2; reject on decode failure.
Recompute HMAC-SHA256 over 'v1.' + part1 using the key identified by payload.kid; constant-time compare against decoded part 2.
Reject if payload.v != 1, key id is unknown, exp <= iat, (exp - iat) exceeds the configured lifetime, or now >= exp.
Reject if method, route, drop, or action do not match the expected values for the current request.
Recompute SHA-256 over the raw forwarded request body and constant-time compare against decoded payload.bodyHash; reject on mismatch.

testVectors.description: Valid cart assertion, test-only key, fixed clock and jti for cross-language determinism.

notes: The test key above is test-only and must never be used outside automated test fixtures.
The origin assertion signing key is dedicated and must not be shared with the admission token or action proof signing keys.
This contract governs origin<->connector trust only; it is unrelated to browser-facing admission and action tokens.
